$comment: Claim statuses and totals derive exclusively from the authoritative 91-claim inventory. This registry records amendment/formalization provenance, conditionality, supporting work and verified source-tree evidence; local full Lean audit is independently reported, not a GitHub Actions pass.

historical.label: Original October 27 manuscript statements
historical.description: Last inventory revision before the November 6 manuscript corrections (PRs #45, #46 and #47). The same file is on main up to dd7138b, the PR #43 merge.

formalizations.scope_change: The original 27 October theorem used c*n^k and was corrected on 6 November to c*max(n,1)^k to cover empty input; the actual original W_M construction and its uniform polynomial-time writer hypotheses are now discharged. This is a proof of the corrected original manuscript statement, not a physical WCT claim.

amendments.scope: Quantifier range corrected from all t ≥ 0 to 0 ≤ t ≤ L(n). The corrected theorem was already kernel-checked; the manuscript now states it.
Same correction: C_{2t} encodes the configuration for 0 ≤ t ≤ L(n), and the two-step identity holds while the head stays in Λ_n.
Time bound corrected from c·n^k to c·max(n,1)^k. With the original bound, n = 0 forced T_M(0) = 0 and P_Turing degenerated to {∅, Σ*}.

Replaced by a conditional obstruction under an unproved common-successor mixing hypothesis. Curvature collapse is not shown to imply the hypothesis; language triviality and rule non-identifiability are no longer claimed.
Quiescence assumption added and the linear bound replaced by |supp C_t| ≤ |supp C_0|(2rt+1)^d. Locality alone does not give superpolynomial time.
Now an explicitly conditional implication in the restricted charged-encoder frozen WCT model. The hypothetical P_TM = NP_TM is not proved, and no universal physical barrier is established.
Now a negative description-size obstruction, K_D(s) ≤ |s|+c. The original state-as-short-witness inference is withdrawn; this is not a lower bound or a separation.

conditional.$comment: Exact means the stated implication is kernel-checked; it does not prove the premises. 'open' = a premise is an unproved complexity hypothesis. 'model' = explicit physical or modelling hypotheses that are assumptions, not theorems. build.js fails if an Exact row whose text mentions a premise, hypothesis, conditionality or an implication is neither listed here nor exempted with a reason.

open.II-24: Assumes polynomial physical resources, the capacity law, uniform simulation with counted update rounds, and P_Turing ≠ NP_Turing.
open.I-1: Verified: (1) curvature cost above every polynomial-time bound together with (2) verifiability implies ψ* ∈ NP \ P (state version). Not proved: premise (1).
open.I-4: Verified: verifiable and not constructible implies ψ* ∈ NP \ P and P ≠ NP (state version). Not proved: premise (2), non-constructibility.
open.I-5: Verified: the class identifications, whose premises are proved for the discrete model, and the implication from a separation to P ≠ NP. Not proved: any such separation.
open.I-9: Verified: a verifier together with every decider exceeding a rail infinitely often implies P^phys ≠ NP^phys. Not proved: the hardness premise for any language.
open.I-10: Verified: under common-successor mixing of the observable transition relation, no nonconstant symbolic readout is invariant. Not proved: the mixing hypothesis, which curvature collapse is not shown to imply.
open.I-12: Verified: in the restricted charged-encoder frozen model, P_TM = NP_TM gives a constant-cost dense SAT implementation, so a barrier there would entail P_TM ≠ NP_TM. Not proved: P_TM = NP_TM or P_TM ≠ NP_TM.
open.I-18: Verified: the conjecture implies dense CNF-SAT ∈ NP_WCC \ P_WCC, hence P_WCC ⊊ NP_WCC. Not proved: the conjecture.
open.I-19: Verified: the conjecture implies P ≠ NP. Not proved: the conjecture.
open.I-21: Verified: substituting an area lower bound and a coercivity bound yields the curvature-cost bound. Not proved: the two input lower bounds for deciders.
open.I-24: Verified: a verifier and the absence of an admissible decider give L ∈ NP^phys \ P^phys. Not proved: the absence of a decider for any language.
open.I-33: Verified: the price inequality and the area-growth hypothesis, both quantified over every decider, give C_Θ(L,n) ≥ κ₀c₀2^{γn}. Not proved: either hypothesis for a concrete language.
open.I-35: Verified: under the same-class identifications, a separation gives P ≠ NP. Not proved: the separation.
open.I-41: Verified: physical NP membership plus asymptotic hardness against every decider gives a physical separation; the fixed-n impossibility remark is unconditional. Not proved: the hardness premise.
open.II-16: Verified: a language in NP^disc \ P^disc implies P ≠ NP. Not proved: the existence of such a language, which the proved class equalities make equivalent to P ≠ NP.

model.II-18: Verified from the manuscript's physical identities, stated as explicit hypotheses. The identities are modelling assumptions, not Lean theorems.
model.II-21: Verified with the independent-lane premise as an explicit hypothesis. The premise is a modelling assumption.
model.II-23: Verified under the explicit counting premise T_W ≤ N_updates + 1 and the capacity premises, which are modelling assumptions.
model.II-27: Verified through phys_step_ceiling, under the same capacity and counting premises as II-23.
model.III-3: Verified: additivity of stored energy and a per-cell minimum c₀ give E_store ≥ n·c₀. Assumed: additivity and the per-cell bound.
model.III-11: Verified: an area lower bound A and the coercivity κ·area ≤ cost give C_Θ ≥ κA. Assumed: both bounds.

exempt.I-13: Unconditional theorem under its stated quiescence and finite-support assumptions.
exempt.I-36: Unconditional: the restricted separation schema is proved equivalent to P ≠ NP; nothing is assumed.
exempt.II-4: Structural theorem with an ordinary hypothesis (quantization compatibility) and a converse construction; no unproved premise.
exempt.III-16: Analytic upper bound under an ordinary uniform H² hypothesis; no unproved premise.

supporting.title: First-answer TM tableau
supporting.statement: For every single-tape machine M, input length n and time t, an explicit bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit outputs M's first answer whenever that answer appears by step t.

supporting.title: Polynomial circuit-size bound
supporting.statement: That circuit has size at most K_M·(t+1)·(4t+2), polynomial in t for a fixed machine.

supporting.title: P_TM ⊆ P/poly
supporting.statement: Every polynomial-time Turing-machine language has polynomial-size circuit families.

supporting.title: Shared-gate CNF certificates
supporting.statement: Every circuit has a linear-size CNF certificate of its evaluation, with one variable per shared gate.

supporting.title: NP verifier circuit families
supporting.statement: Every NP_TM language has polynomial-size verifier circuits over the input and a padded certificate.

supporting.title: Non-uniform NP-to-dense-SAT projections
supporting.statement: Every NP_TM language reduces to SAT_dense by polynomial-size literal projections. No machine is claimed to compute them, so this is not CL-1.

supporting.title: SAT circuit lower-bound equivalence
supporting.statement: SAT_dense ∉ P/poly if and only if NP_TM ⊄ P/poly. Neither side is proved.

supporting.title: Matrix SAT encoding
supporting.statement: The packed matrix instance word(S, U) is in SAT_dense exactly when some entry of S is not in U.

supporting.title: Matrix crossing-sequence inequality
supporting.statement: Any single-tape machine deciding SAT_dense in time T satisfies (G(n)+1)·ℓ ≤ 2·T(N(n)) under the stated counting condition.

supporting.title: Quadratic hard-input family
supporting.statement: Every correct single-tape SAT_dense decider has arbitrarily long rejected inputs x with |x|² ≤ 384·b_M·time_M(x). This quadratic, machine-dependent bound is far from superpolynomial.

supporting.title: Restricted matrix-family circuit
supporting.statement: On valid packed matrix instances, a single-layer circuit of size at most 1+4n·2^n decides membership, so this hard-input family cannot yield circuit lower bounds.

supporting.title: Uniform SAT decision transfer
supporting.statement: The uniform construction proves SAT_dense ∉ P_TM if and only if P_TM ≠ NP_TM. The separation itself remains open.

supporting.title: Negated toroidal seam
supporting.statement: The dense encoding of a finite equality ring with a negated seam is unsatisfiable at every ring length. The seam bit determines the answer on this family.

supporting.title: Ordinary toroidal seam
supporting.statement: The dense encoding of the same ring with an ordinary seam has a constant satisfying assignment.

open.title: Superpolynomial SAT circuit lower bound
open.statement: SAT_dense ∉ P/poly. With P_TM ⊆ P/poly (proved) it would imply SATLowerBound, but it is a strictly stronger, non-uniform statement.
open.formal: Stated as a hypothesis; not proved

open.title: CrossingSAT.SATLowerBound
open.statement: SAT_dense ∉ P_TM: no polynomial-time single-tape machine decides dense CNF-SAT. This is the central unresolved theorem of the program.
open.formal: Defined as a Prop; not proved

open.title: Classical P_TM ≠ NP_TM
open.statement: Uniform Cook–Levin gives SATLowerBound ↔ P_TM ≠ NP_TM. An unconditional proof of either side remains open.
